signals.signal: ESMA statement ESMA75-113276571-1679 (17/04/2026) confirms the MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets, Reg (EU) 2023/1114) transitional/grandfathering regime expired EU-wide on 01/07/2026 with no extension. Any entity serving EU clients without a CASP (Crypto-Asset Service Provider - a firm licensed to hold, exchange, transfer or execute orders in crypto for clients) licence is in breach of EU law; unauthorised CASPs must have executed a wind-down plan by that date; NCAs (national competent authorities) are instructed to verify wind-down plans, take action against unauthorised provision, and scrutinise client-migration. ESMA also states non-EU entities may not serve EU clients outside narrow reverse solicitation, and CASPs may not outsource/delegate custody to non-authorised third-country entities.
signals.source_name: ESMA - Statement on the End of Transitional Periods under MiCA (PDF)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every footprint bank that holds fiat accounts for, or settles for, crypto firms - Erste, RBI, UniCredit, OTP, Alpha, NBG, Piraeus, BCR, Banca Transilvania, Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic Bank. (b) They must re-paper and re-screen every crypto counterparty against the ESMA register and offboard unlicensed ones -> AML/KYC screening and counterparty risk (IMTF Siron, FICO), INETCO transaction monitoring across the crypto/fiat boundary, Namirial eKYC re-verification of migrated crypto clients. (c) Budget is being committed NOW; the enforcement wave is H2-2026/H1-2027.
signals.likelihood: Certain - already in force; NCA enforcement over next 6-12 months
signals.followup: Ask Alpha Bank (existing Siron customer) and Bank of Cyprus whether CASP counterparty re-screening is inside Siron or manual.

signals.signal: ESMA interim MiCA register (CASPS.csv, last updated 31/07/2026) lists 323 authorised CASPs across 26 EEA home states. Footprint split: Cyprus 25 (CySEC), Austria 11 (FMA), Czechia 11 (CNB), Croatia 6 (HANFA + HNB), Slovakia 6 (NBS), Bulgaria 4 (FSC), Slovenia 3 (ATVP), and ZERO in Greece, Hungary and Romania. The ART register (ARTZZ.csv - asset-referenced tokens, i.e. stablecoins backed by a basket) is EMPTY EU-wide: no ART issuer is authorised anywhere. 41 EMT (e-money token - a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to a single official currency) white-paper records exist; none from a footprint issuer, three are Czech (Payment Corporation SE / Stable Labs); bank-issued EMTs so far are French (Societe Generale-Forge, and CACEIS BANK SA notified 30/06/2026).
signals.source_name: ESMA Interim MiCA Register - CASPS.csv / ARTZZ.csv / EMTWP.csv
signals.implies: (a) Affected: the 66 licensed CASPs headquartered in the footprint plus the banks that serve them. (b) Each licensed CASP is now a supervised obliged entity needing onboarding/eKYC, AML screening, Travel-Rule data completeness and DORA-grade ICT - Namirial digital onboarding and IMTF Siron AML sold directly to CASPs is a NEW non-bank buyer segment for Printec, concentrated in Cyprus and Czechia. (c) Buying now; the register grows weekly so the target list refreshes weekly.
signals.followup: Automate a weekly pull of CASPS.csv, build a Cyprus/Czechia/Austria CASP target list for Namirial + Siron.

signals.signal: HPB - Croatia's largest domestically-owned bank - was authorised as a MiCA CASP by the CROATIAN NATIONAL BANK (HNB) on 16/06/2026 per the ESMA register (competent authority field: 'Croatian National Bank'). It is the ONLY credit institution in the 17-country footprint currently on the ESMA CASP register. Croatia splits MiCA competence: HANFA for CASPs and Titles II, V and VI; HNB for Titles III and IV (ART/EMT issuance) and for credit institutions.
signals.source_name: ESMA Interim MiCA Register CASPS.csv; ESMA List of Competent Authorities notified to ESMA under MiCA (PDF)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: HPB directly, and by competitive follow-on Zagrebacka/PBZ, Erste Croatia (existing OptiCash customer), OTP Croatia. (b) A bank offering crypto services must protect private keys to HSM standard, segregate client crypto, prove reserves, and run crypto-aware AML -> Thales HSM/PCI and remote key injection, IMTF Siron with virtual-asset typologies, INETCO monitoring at the fiat/crypto boundary, Namirial eKYC. (c) HPB is spending now; peer banks should commit budget within 6-12 months (H1-2027).
signals.followup: Obtain HPB's crypto-custody architecture; use it as the reference when approaching Erste Croatia and PBZ.

signals.signal: MNB issued Hungary's FIRST MiCA CASP licence on 20/07/2026 to Tiwala Solutions Kft (CoinCash), covering six services (custody, crypto-fiat exchange, crypto-crypto exchange, transfer, advice, portfolio management). In parallel the Hungarian Parliament voted 143-46 to repeal the domestic crypto 'validation declaration' requirement that had made Hungary one of the EU's strictest regimes and had frozen the market. Hungary used only a 6-MONTH MiCA grandfathering period (per ESMA's Art.143(3) list), i.e. it ended 01/07/2025 - a year before the EU backstop - which is why Hungary had zero licensed CASPs until now. The entity is not yet reflected in the 31/07/2026 ESMA register extract.
signals.source_name: Portfolio.hu, 'Fordulat a hazai kriptopiacon: megszerezte a szukseges engedelyt' [Turnaround in the domestic crypto market: it has obtained the necessary licence] (press); ESMA List of MiCA grandfathering periods Art.143(3) (regulator)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: OTP, MKB, Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary - they will be asked to bank newly licensed Hungarian CASPs, and MNB will supervise the relationship. (b) Buy: Siron AML with VASP counterparty typologies, Namirial eKYC, card issuing/POS acquiring for crypto-to-card off-ramps. (c) Budget commit H2-2026 to H1-2027 as the Hungarian market restarts.
signals.followup: Find the MNB primary press release or MNB institution-register entry for Tiwala Solutions - the MNB 2026 press-release index did not surface July items to the fetch tool.

signals.signal: CySEC press release of 23/12/2025 set 27/02/2026 as the hard deadline for Cypriot CASPs to APPLY for MiCA authorisation; non-applicants had to file a wind-down plan and cease crypto services by 01/07/2026. CySEC explicitly reminded registered CASPs that Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 (the crypto Travel Rule) obligations continue to apply throughout, and that cross-border provision into another Member State is only possible where that host state's grandfathering permits. Cyprus took the full 18-month grandfathering; result: 25 authorised Cypriot CASPs at 31/07/2026 - the largest footprint concentration and 4th largest in the EEA (after DE 68, FR 35, NL 29).
signals.source_name: CySEC - Press Release 'MiCA licence applications due by 27 February 2026' (PDF)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: 25 licensed Cypriot CASPs plus Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic Bank and Eurobank Cyprus as their banking counterparties. (b) The CASPs must buy Travel-Rule-capable screening, eKYC and AML; the banks must buy enhanced due diligence and monitoring -> Namirial eKYC + IMTF Siron at CASPs; Siron/FICO + INETCO at banks. (c) Deadline already passed - spend is live in 2026.
signals.followup: Bank of Cyprus is an existing Glory TCR customer - use that relationship as the entry point for crypto-counterparty AML.

signals.entity: FMA Austria / NBS Slovakia / ATVP Slovenia / CNB Czechia
signals.signal: ESMA's official Art.143(3) list shows footprint Member States chose DIFFERENT grandfathering lengths, all measured from 30/12/2024: 18 months (ended 01/07/2026) for Bulgaria, Czechia, Greece, Croatia, Cyprus, Romania, Luxembourg, Malta; 12 months (ended 30/12/2025) for AUSTRIA and SLOVAKIA; 6 months (ended 01/07/2025) for HUNGARY and SLOVENIA. Austria's FMA had authorised 11 CASPs by 31/07/2026 (latest OSL EU GmbH 07/07/2026); Czechia's CNB 11 (latest Altlift s.r.o. 30/06/2026); Slovakia's NBS 6 (all Dec-2025/Jan-2026); Slovenia's ATVP 3.

signals.implies: (a) Affected: Erste Group and RBI (AT), Slovenska sporitelna/Tatra banka (SK), NLB/NKBM (SI), CSOB/Komercni (CZ) - all now bank a licensed, supervised CASP population. signals.signal: ESMA's official 'List of Competent Authorities notified to ESMA under MiCA' still records Romania as 'TBA' for its MiCA competent authorities, and the ESMA register shows ZERO authorised Romanian CASPs at 31/07/2026 - despite Romania having taken the full 18-month grandfathering that ended 01/07/2026. Law-firm sources (corroboration only) state MiCA was transposed by Government Emergency Ordinance (OUG) 10/2025 in force 13/03/2025, naming ASF for CASPs and BNR for EMT issuers, with a 0.5% monthly supervisory fee on CASP revenue.
signals.source_name: ESMA - List of Competent Authorities notified to ESMA under MiCA (PDF); ESMA CASPS.csv
signals.implies: (a) Affected: BCR (APTRA customer), BRD, Banca Transilvania, Raiffeisen Romania. (b) With no licensed domestic CASP, Romanian retail crypto activity flows to foreign passported CASPs - the hardest pattern for a bank to see. Banks must buy card-and-transfer level detection of crypto on-/off-ramps: INETCO transaction monitoring plus Siron/FICO AML rules keyed to foreign CASP IBANs and card MCCs. (c) Budget commit H2-2026 for 2027 delivery.
signals.likelihood: Medium - first ASF authorisations plausible within 6-12 months

signals.entity: Hellenic Capital Market Commission (HCMC) / Bank of Greece
signals.signal: Greece transposed MiCA via Law 5193/2025, designating the HCMC (Epitropi Kefalaiagoras) as competent authority for CASPs, introducing sanctions for the professional provision of crypto services without a licence, and adding investor and whistleblower protections; HCMC Decision No. 8/1059 of 30/07/2025 set out the CASP authorisation procedure. Greece took the full 18-month grandfathering, which ended 01/07/2026. Despite this, ZERO Greek CASPs appear on the ESMA register at 31/07/2026. ESMA's competent-authority list confirms HCMC for Greece; the Bank of Greece handles ART/EMT prudential aspects.
signals.source_name: ESMA List of Competent Authorities notified under MiCA (regulator) + EY Greece tax alert on the MiCA authorisation procedure / HCMC Decision 8/1059 (press corroboration)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Alpha Bank, NBG, Piraeus, Eurobank. (b) Greece has live sanctions for unlicensed crypto provision but no domestic licensed CASP, so all Greek crypto flow is cross-border - banks must detect it at the payment/card layer -> INETCO monitoring plus a crypto-counterparty typology pack on Alpha Bank's existing IMTF Siron deployment (a direct upsell into an installed base). (c) Budget H2-2026.
signals.followup: Retrieve Law 5193/2025 from the FEK and HCMC Decision 8/1059 from hcmc.gr; do NOT quote Greek sanction levels until the FEK text is read.

ESMA's Art.143(3) footnote records that entities added to the Bulgarian VASP register between 30/12/2024 and 08/07/2025 had to apply for MiCA authorisation before 08/10/2025. signals.implies: (a) Affected: UniCredit Bulbank, DSK, Postbank, plus the four licensed CASPs. (b) Bulgaria adopted the euro on 01/01/2026, so euro-denominated EMTs now sit directly alongside domestic retail payments and BNB is the EMT authority - banks need EMT-aware AML and CASP counterparty controls -> Siron, INETCO, Namirial eKYC. (c) Two of the four licences are three weeks old: spend is live now.
signals.followup: Check the BNB site for any Title IV EMT authorisation guidance and whether any Bulgarian bank has notified an EMT white paper.

signals.signal: The Commission opened a TARGETED CONSULTATION ON THE REVIEW OF MiCA on 20/05/2026, closing 30/09/2026 23:59 CEST. It feeds the report mandated by MiCA Articles 140 and 142, which 'may, if warranted, be accompanied by a new legislative proposal to amend and complement this regulation'. Live topics include centralising CASP supervision at ESMA and away from national regulators, stablecoin/EMT-ART treatment, and third-country multi-issuer stablecoin schemes. Separately, MiCA Art.140(2)(v) requires the Commission, with EBA and ESMA, to report to the co-legislators BY JUNE 2027 on whether a third-country equivalence regime is needed.
signals.source_name: European Commission - Targeted consultation on the review of MiCA Regulation (+ consultation document PDF)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every footprint bank or CASP building crypto capability, and Printec's own product roadmap. (b) A 'MiCA-2' proposal is realistically 2027, meaning a second compliance cycle - argue for configurable, rule-driven AML/monitoring platforms (Siron, INETCO, FICO) over hard-coded builds, and modular HSM key management. (c) No procurement deadline; shapes 2027-2028 budgets. Printec/its bank customers can respond to the consultation until 30/09/2026.
signals.likelihood: High that a legislative proposal follows in 2027
signals.followup: Read the consultation document PDF (finance.ec.europa.eu/document/download/62be7015-f066-4fac-b74e-71bacdbcc9f5_en) for the specific supervision-centralisation questions.

signals.entity: ESMA - Common Supervisory Action on CASP digital operational resilience (custody)

Executing NCAs across the footprint: CySEC, CNB, FMA, HANFA/HNB, NBS-SK, FSC, ATVP, HCMC, MNB and (once notified) ASF.

signals.implies: (a) Affected: all 66 footprint CASPs plus HPB (the one bank CASP). (b) They must evidence private-key management, client-asset segregation, ICT third-party risk and incident response under DORA -> Thales HSM/PCI and remote key injection for custody keys, documented key ceremonies delivered by Printec managed/field services, ICT resilience evidence packs. (c) Budget must commit in H2-2026 to be ready for on-site review in H1-2027.
signals.followup: Find the ESMA primary CSA announcement on esma.europa.eu/press-news - only an aggregator was reachable this run; do not quote scope wording until the ESMA text is read.

signals.entity: Qivalis (bank consortium euro stablecoin) / Raiffeisen Bank International / UniCredit
signals.country: Austria (+ footprint via RBI and UniCredit networks)

Members announced 02/12/2025 include RAIFFEISEN BANK INTERNATIONAL (Austria), UNICREDIT, ING, KBC, CaixaBank, DekaBank, Danske Bank, SEB and Banca Sella, with BNP Paribas joining 01/12/2025; press reports membership grew to ~37 banks across 15 countries during 2026, and that reserves will be at least 40% bank deposits with the balance in high-quality liquid bonds. A live bank euro-stablecoin pushes token handling into their CEE subsidiaries. (b) Buy: Thales HSM + remote key injection for wallet/treasury keys, IMTF Siron/FICO AML rules for EMT flows, INETCO monitoring; longer term crypto/EMT cash-out at ATM and kiosk on x-core, and cash automation to service the fiat leg. signals.entity: EBA Travel Rule Guidelines (EBA/GL/2024/11) under Reg (EU) 2023/1113
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2024] Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 recast the funds-transfer regulation and extended the FATF 'travel rule' (the obligation to send originator and beneficiary identity data with a transfer) to crypto-asset transfers with NO de-minimis threshold - every crypto transfer must carry names, wallet/account numbers and identifiers, and transfers of EUR 1,000 or more to/from self-hosted wallets require additional ownership-verification checks. It also subjects CASPs to the same AML/CFT requirements and supervision as credit and financial institutions. EBA published its Travel Rule Guidelines on 04/07/2024, applying from 30/12/2024; they set out what PSPs, intermediary PSPs, CASPs and intermediary CASPs must do to detect missing or incomplete information and how to handle non-compliant transfers. Forward trigger: AMLA becomes operational and crypto is a named priority risk area, with AMLA direct supervision of the largest cross-border firms from 2028 and AMLR (Reg (EU) 2024/1624) applying from 10/07/2027.
signals.source_name: EBA - 'EBA issues Travel Rule guidance to tackle money laundering and terrorist financing in transfers of funds and crypto assets' + Travel Rule Guidelines PDF
signals.implies: (a) Affected: every footprint bank acting as PSP or intermediary PSP on the fiat leg of a crypto transfer, and every licensed CASP. (b) They must run automated completeness checks, missing-data handling and sanctions/AML screening on both fiat and crypto legs -> IMTF Siron and FICO for screening and case management, INETCO for real-time transaction monitoring, Namirial eKYC for the identity data itself. (c) The Travel Rule is already binding; the AMLR budget wave must commit by H2-2026 to be delivered before 10/07/2027.
signals.followup: This overlaps Agent 3's AML/AMLA workstream - deconflict so the AMLR 10/07/2027 date is stated once. For any data-subject-rights or personal-data-breach question arising from Travel Rule data sharing, do not give a ruling - refer to Printec's DPO / Compliance team.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (CBK/BQK)
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025, with the compliance window running into 2026] CBK's Board approved on 29/08/2025 the 'Regulation on Licensing of Crypto-Assets Service Operators Providing Crypto-Assets Exchange Services', made under Law No. 08/L-295 on Crypto-Assets and drafted on the basis of MiCA. Article 23: the regulation enters into force 90 days after Board approval; Article 21: institutions subject to licensing must, within 90 days of entry into force, take all necessary actions to apply and comply. Critically, Article 1.1 expressly brings CRYPTO ATMs ('including crypto ATMs or cryptocurrency ATMs') with a physical office base inside the licensing perimeter. Breaches attract corrective measures and administrative penalties under Art.67 of Law 03/L-209 and Chapter VII of Law 08/L-295.
signals.source_name: CBK/BQK - Regulation on Licensing of Crypto-Assets Service Operators Providing Crypto-Assets Exchange Services (EN PDF)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Kosovo crypto exchange operators and crypto-ATM deployers, plus Kosovo banks (Raiffeisen Kosovo, ProCredit, NLB, TEB) that will bank them. (b) Kosovo is the ONLY footprint market that explicitly licenses CRYPTO ATMs - a regulated self-service estate Printec can address directly with NCR/self-service kiosks, Namirial eKYC capture at the machine, cash automation/recycling, ATM telemetry and monitoring, physical ATM security and managed field services. (c) The application window has already run - licensed operators are deploying now.
signals.followup: Ask CBK for the public register of licensed crypto-asset service operators and the crypto-ATM count; scope a compliant kiosk + eKYC offer. bqk-kos.org HTML is Cloudflare-blocked to the fetch tool but PDFs download fine with a desktop UA.

signals.entity: Ministry of Finance / AMF / Bank of Albania
signals.signal: Albania is running TWO parallel crypto workstreams. (1) A new crypto-asset framework law of 142 articles, modelled on MiCA, splitting competence between the AMF (Financial Supervisory Authority - licensing and market supervision of service providers) and the BANK OF ALBANIA (e-money tokens, monetary stability and payment-system implications); reported to be intended to enter into force 01/03/2026 with subsidiary acts fully operational in spring 2027. (2) A NEW draft law released for public consultation by the Ministry of Finance and reported on 19/07/2026 imposing MANDATORY CRYPTO-ASSET REPORTING to the tax authorities: crypto-asset service providers must register with a unique identifier, archive transaction data for not less than 7 years, and report; fines of 100,000 to 1,000,000 leke for failure to register, failure to report on time, or inaccurate reporting; the AMF must notify the General Tax Directorate within 10 days of any licensing, suspension or revocation; an 80m leke state-funded electronic reporting system is envisaged; the reporting/automatic-exchange effects are stated to begin on Albania's EU accession.
signals.source_name: Top Channel, 'Kripto-asetet ne lupen e tatimeve/ Projektligj i ri per raportim te detyrueshem ne organet tatimore, gjoba deri ne 1 mln leke' [Crypto-assets under the tax microscope: new draft law on mandatory reporting to tax authorities, fines up to 1m leke] (press)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Albanian crypto operators and the banks that serve them - Raiffeisen Albania and OTP Albania are Printec reference customers. (b) A 7-year transaction-archive plus structured reporting obligation is a document-management and reporting-platform requirement, on top of eKYC (unique identifier registration) and AML -> Printec document management, Namirial eKYC, Siron AML. Bank of Albania competence over e-money tokens also flags a future EMT/payment-rails workstream. (c) Draft stage - budget signal for 2027, monitor adoption.
signals.followup: Verify in Fletorja Zyrtare whether the 142-article crypto-asset law was actually adopted and in force from 01/03/2026 - only Albanian press was reachable. Check bankofalbania.org and amf.gov.al for the official consultation text before quoting the leke fine band.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (NBS) / Securities Commission
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2020, unchanged] Serbia still regulates crypto under the domestic Law on Digital Assets (RS Official Gazette No 153/2020), NOT MiCA. Competence is split: NBS licenses and supervises VIRTUAL CURRENCY services and maintains the public Register of virtual currency service providers plus the decisions granting licences; the Securities Commission handles digital tokens; where an asset has both characteristics, competence is shared. The Serbian Act contains a definition of stablecoins but NO substantive stablecoin-specific provisions - general crypto-asset rules apply, unlike MiCA's EMT/ART split. No MiCA-alignment amendment has been published.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Serbia - Digital assets (supervision) page and Register of virtual currency service providers
signals.implies: (a) Affected: Raiffeisen Serbia (x-core customer), AikBank (NCR recyclers), Banca Intesa Beograd, UniCredit Serbia. (b) Serbia's EU accession chapter work and the MONEYVAL/National Risk Assessment finding of virtual-asset vulnerabilities mean a MiCA-style rewrite is coming - Serbian banks will then need EMT-aware AML and CASP counterparty controls. Today the concrete buy is AML/KYC (Siron) covering NBS-licensed virtual currency providers as counterparties. (c) No hard deadline; watch for a draft amendment - budget 2027+.
signals.likelihood: Medium that a MiCA-aligned draft appears within 12-18 months
signals.followup: Pull the NBS Register of virtual currency service providers from dataexchange.nbs.rs to size the Serbian licensed population; watch Sluzbeni glasnik for amendments to the Law on Digital Assets.

signals.signal: The three remaining Western Balkans footprint markets are all still PRE-LICENSING. Montenegro: PM Spajic announced in Sep-2025 that a MiCA-conforming law would be adopted and the finance ministry launched a public consultation; the CBCG participates in interagency working groups but the law was still not adopted as of mid-2026. North Macedonia: government plans announced to introduce a VASP/exchange licensing regime aligned to MiCA during 2026, with first licences possible in 2026 subject to parliamentary adoption. Bosnia & Herzegovina remains a three-way split - Republika Srpska has recognised virtual currencies since Oct-2022 under its amended Law on the Securities Market (RS Securities Commission), Brcko District adopted a new Securities Market Law in March 2026 creating space for virtual-asset regulation but with no implementing regulations yet, and a proposed Federation FinTech Bill (Q4-2025) would create entity-wide VASP licensing including the FATF Travel Rule.
signals.source_name: Crypto for Innovation, 'Montenegro Takes Tentative Steps Towards Crypto Regulation'; CEE Legal Matters, 'North Macedonia: A Path Toward Regulating Crypto Markets'; General Bytes, 'Bosnia and Herzegovina: A Three-Way Regulatory Split' (all aggregator/press)
signals.implies: (a) Affected: CKB/Erste Montenegro, NLB and Komercijalna in ME; Stopanska, Komercijalna and NLB in MK; UniCredit, Raiffeisen and Intesa in BiH. (b) When these regimes land, each will require a licensed-VASP register, Travel Rule data handling and eKYC - the same Siron/Namirial/INETCO stack Printec already sells into these banks; BiH's three-way split means three separate compliance builds per group. (c) Too early for procurement - watch for the Montenegrin and Macedonian bills reaching parliament; budget signal 2027.
signals.likelihood: Medium for a Montenegrin or Macedonian law within 12 months
signals.followup: Check cbcg.me and nbrm.mk news pages (desktop UA) monthly for a published draft; get the Brcko District Securities Market Law text of March 2026 from the Brcko official gazette.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no prior checkpoint for 02/08/2026; MiCA was untouched by the 24/07/2026 baseline, so all of this is new ground). Sources actually opened: ESMA statement PDF ESMA75-113276571-1679 (17/04/2026); ESMA interim MiCA register raw files CASPS.csv (323 rows, last update 31/07/2026), ARTZZ.csv (empty), EMTWP.csv (41 rows) - parsed locally to derive the per-country footprint counts, the HPB/HNB entry and the absence of GR/HU/RO; ESMA 'List of grandfathering periods under Art.143(3)' PDF; ESMA 'List of Competent Authorities notified under MiCA' PDF (source of the Romania 'TBA' finding); CySEC press release PDF 23/12/2025; European Commission MiCA review consultation page; EBA Travel Rule press release; CaixaBank Qivalis release; CBK/BQK Kosovo licensing regulation PDF (crypto-ATM perimeter); NBS Serbia digital-assets page; minfin.com.ua (UA); Top Channel (AL); Portfolio.hu (HU). Local-language sweep done in Hungarian (kriptoeszkoz-szolgaltato engedely - MNB/CoinCash), Ukrainian (virtualnykh aktyviv zakon 2026), Albanian (ligj kripto-asetet, projektligj AMF/BSh), German (MiCAR Uebergangsfrist FMA), Bulgarian (kriptoaktivi litsenz KFN), Romanian (furnizori servicii cripto ASF), Croatian (kriptoimovina HNB/Hanfa), Greek (paroxoi kryptostoicheion HCMC). Genuine gaps: (1) no primary MNB text for the 20/07/2026 CoinCash licence - MNB's press index did not surface July items; (2) no ESMA primary page for the crypto-custody Common Supervisory Action - aggregator only, hence Low confidence; (3) Greek Law 5193/2025 and HCMC Decision 8/1059 not read in the original FEK, so no sanction figures are quoted; (4) Romanian OUG 10/2025 not read in Monitorul Oficial, so the ASF/BNR split and the 0.5% supervisory fee are marked Low and flagged for verification; (5) Albanian 142-article law adoption status not confirmed in Fletorja Zyrtare; (6) no primary confirmation that DNB has granted Qivalis its EMI licence. Deliberate non-claims: no fine levels, no holding limits and no ART authorisations are asserted anywhere, because no primary source supported them.
access_issues: fma.gv.at (both DE and EN URLs) returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch and a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' interstitial to curl even with a desktop Chrome User-Agent and de-AT Accept-Language - Austrian CASP counts were therefore derived from the ESMA register instead of the FMA Unternehmensdatenbank; route not yet escalated to Claude-in-Chrome. bqk-kos.org HTML news page returns the same Cloudflare 403 with a desktop UA, but the underlying PDF (https://bqk-kos.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ENG-Rregullore-per-licencimin-e-operatoreve-te-kripto-aseteve.pdf?lang=en) downloads cleanly with a desktop UA and was extracted locally with pdfminer - that is the working route for BQK. pdftotext is not installed on this machine; all PDFs were extracted with python3 pdfminer.six. hnb.hr/en/o-nama/kriptoimovina and mnb.hu press indexes returned navigation shells only (JS-rendered lists), so the HPB and CoinCash facts rest on the ESMA register and Hungarian press respectively. The ESMA MiCA landing page returned only the register update date to WebFetch; the raw CSV/PDF asset URLs were scraped from the HTML with curl and parsed locally, which is the reliable route for ESMA register data.
